description: Revenue/Sales Analytics - Admin gets a detailed analytics command showing daily, weekly, and monthly sales breakdown, top products, top buyers, and revenue trends. Accessible via a new button in the admin menu.
steps: Add new button BTN_ADM_ANALYTICS = _b('📈 Analytics') in the admin buttons section around line 690.
Add BTN_ADM_ANALYTICS to admin_main_kb() layout - place it paired with BTN_ADM_ORDER_LOOKUP on the same row, moving BTN_ADM_SETTINGS to its own row before HOME_BTN.

Create async def get_analytics_data() function in the Firebase helpers section. It should: (a) fetch all orders, vpn_orders, proxy_orders, (b) compute today's revenue/count, this week's revenue/count, this month's revenue/count using created_at timestamps, (c) find top 5 products by total_sold, (d) find top 5 buyers by total_spent.

Create def fmt_analytics(data: dict) -> str formatting function that displays: Today (revenue, orders), This Week (revenue, orders), This Month (revenue, orders), Top Products table, Top Buyers table. Use _SEP separator and HTML bold formatting.
Add handler in router_admin for BTN_ADM_ANALYTICS at AdminFlow.menu state: call get_analytics_data(), format with fmt_analytics(), reply with admin_main_kb().
Register the handler properly so it responds when admin presses the Analytics button from admin menu.
acceptance_criteria: python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('bot.py').read())" passes without errors
BTN_ADM_ANALYTICS button exists and is in admin_main_kb()
fmt_analytics() produces a well-formatted HTML message
Admin can press Analytics button from admin menu and see stats
verification: python3 -c "import ast; tree = ast.parse(open('bot.py').read()); funcs = [n.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]; assert 'get_analytics_data' in funcs; assert 'fmt_analytics' in funcs; print('Analytics functions OK')"
